question_text:
A 54-year-old woman presents to the physician with discomfort in her upper left abdomen over the past month. Moreover, she has recently been feeling a bit tired. She has no history of any significant illness and takes no medications. Her vital signs are within normal limits. On percussion, the spleen size is 15 cm (5.9 in). Otherwise, the physical examination shows no abnormalities. The laboratory test results are as follows:
Hemoglobin 10 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 88 μm3
Leukocyte count 65,000/mm3
Platelet count 500,000/mm3
Two images of the peripheral blood smear are shown. Laboratory studies are most likely to show which of the following?

        ### Question
        A 54-year-old woman presents to the physician with discomfort in her upper left abdomen over the past month. Moreover, she has recently been feeling a bit tired. She has no history of any significant illness and takes no medications. Her vital signs are within normal limits. On percussion, the spleen size is 15 cm (5.9 in). Hemoglobin 10 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 88 μm3
Leukocyte count 65,000/mm3
Platelet count 500,000/mm3
Two images of the peripheral blood smear are shown. Laboratory studies are most likely to show which of the following?

        ### Options
        opa. Auer rods
opb. Cluster of differentiation 20 (CD20)
opc. JAK2 mutation
opd. Philadelphia chromosome
ope. Translocation between chromosomes 15 and 17
